objective: Track multiple remembered devices per user so authentication can recognize a previously verified device without treating an IP address as a device identity.
acceptance_criteria: Start gate: a separate Director-owned policy/scope PR has merged to authorize the code agent to write only the required backend/alembic/versions/** migration path. Current code_agent policy denies that path; this task does not change .ai/policy.json or widen any role itself.

A users-owned remembered-device relation stores multiple records per user with a bigint identity primary key, a foreign key to users.id, a unique per-user hash of an opaque high-entropy device id, created_at, last_seen_at and nullable revoked_at. No device record stores a password, Cognito token, raw device id, IP address or geolocation.

The system can register, recognize, update last_seen_at for, and revoke one device without overwriting or forgetting other devices for the same user. A revoked, missing, malformed or unknown device id is never recognized.

The raw device id is generated with a cryptographically secure random source and is returned only as a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookie scoped to the host and root path. The database stores only its hash. Replacing or clearing the cookie cannot make an unrecognized device trusted.

A user's latest device can be derived by ordering that user's device rows by last_seen_at. Do not add a single last_login_device or last_login_location field to users; one field cannot distinguish multiple known devices.

IP address, geolocation, user-agent and browser characteristics are not identity keys. They may only be considered risk context by AUTH-003; persist none of them in the device table. Any future retention of those signals requires a separate privacy/security decision.

Tests cover multiple simultaneous devices, per-user uniqueness, revoked and unknown ids, hash-only persistence, timestamp updates, user deletion/cascade behavior, and the database migration. No UI, email challenge or IP fingerprinting is introduced by this task.
wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x01-users.md records the remembered-device relation and privacy boundary.
